intent: To demonstrate that vaccination rates among Black Americans have converged with those of White and Hispanic Americans over the course of the outbreak.

units.meaning: Early in the outbreak, Black adults (15%) were below White adults (21%) and Hispanic adults (16%); the Black–White gap was 6 points and the Black–Hispanic gap was 1 point.
units.computation: Black−White = 15−21 = −6 percentage points; Black−Hispanic = 15−16 = −1 percentage point
accepted_routes: Early on, Black adults (15%) trailed White (21%) and Hispanic (16%) adults.
At the start, Black vaccination rate was 6 points below White and 1 point below Hispanic.
Initially Black Americans were a bit less likely than White or Hispanic Americans to have had or intend a vaccine.
units.visual_evidence_rule: First/early time point must show Black below White and Hispanic, with 15%, 21%, and 16% visible or readable.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the early Black–White/Hispanic gap?

units.meaning: Black vaccination rate rose from 15% early to 70% at the final period, an increase of 55 percentage points.
accepted_routes: Black vaccination rate rose from 15% to 70% over the outbreak.
Black rate increased by 55 percentage points.
Black adults moved from about 15% early to about 70% at the end.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Black series must start near 15% and end near 70%; if quantified, annotation/label should show +55 pts.
units.temporal_anchor: we've seen a change here... over the course of the outbreak
units.reviewer_question: Is the magnitude of Black increase required to establish convergence?

units.meaning: At the final period, Black, White, and Hispanic rates all reach comparable majority levels: Black 70%, White 72%, Hispanic 76%, a 6-point range with all at least 70%.
accepted_routes: By the end, comparable majorities of Black (70%), White (72%), and Hispanic (76%) adults reported vaccination.
Final Black, White, and Hispanic rates are all around 70%–76%.
The final B/W/H spread is only 6 points, with Black at 70% and Hispanic at 76%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Final time point must show Black, White, and Hispanic close together and at or above 70%, with labels 70, 72, and 76 or equivalent.
units.temporal_anchor: We now find that comparable majorities...
units.reviewer_question: Is final-period comparability/threshold among Black, White, and Hispanic obligatory?

units.meaning: The Black–White gap narrowed from 6 percentage points early to 2 points at the final period; Black closed 4 points, or about two-thirds, of its initial gap with White.
units.computation: Early gap = 21−15 = 6; final gap = 72−70 = 2; narrowing = 6−2 = 4 points; 4/6 = 66.7% of initial gap closed
accepted_routes: The Black–White gap shrank from 6 points to 2 points.
Black closed 4 of the 6 initial points behind White.
About 67% of the early Black–White gap was gone by the end.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Chart must allow comparing Black and White at early and final periods, e.g., two lines/bars showing 21 vs 15 and 72 vs 70.
units.temporal_anchor: we've seen a change here... over the course of the outbreak
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the narrowing Black–White gap, not just final levels?

units.meaning: White and Hispanic vaccination rates also rose substantially: White from 21% to 72% (+51 points) and Hispanic from 16% to 76% (+60 points).
units.computation: White: 72−21 = +51 percentage points; Hispanic: 76−16 = +60 percentage points
accepted_routes: White rose from 21% to 72%, and Hispanic from 16% to 76%.
White increased by 51 points; Hispanic by 60 points.
Both White and Hispanic rates also climbed sharply over the outbreak.
units.visual_evidence_rule: If included, White and Hispanic series must start at 21%/16% and end at 72%/76%.
units.temporal_anchor: over the course of the outbreak
units.reviewer_question: Are White/Hispanic trajectories required, or only Black's trajectory plus final comparison?

optional_valid: Asian* ends highest at 94%, but the intent does not require covering Asian.
Final order among Black/White/Hispanic: Hispanic 76% > White 72% > Black 70%.
Middle listed period values: Black 60%, White 65%, Hispanic 68%, all already majority levels.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that vaccination campaigns or outreach caused the convergence.
Extrapolating beyond the three listed periods or to groups not in the table.
Claiming the Black–Hispanic gap narrowed; the table shows Black 15 vs Hispanic 16 early and Black 70 vs Hispanic 76 final, so that gap went from 1 to 6 points.
Using Asian 94% to say Black/White/Hispanic converged with Asian or that all groups reached 94%.
Saying all groups are equal at the end; Black 70%, White 72%, and Hispanic 76% are comparable but not equal.
notes: The table has no explicit x labels; I treated the three rows per entity as early/mid/final in listed order, matching the narration’s earlier/now/over-outbreak language. Asian* is present in the table but outside the intent; its 94% endpoint should not be used to claim Black/White/Hispanic convergence.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
